It booked an HBM system in Q4 and more in January for Q1 (the transcript wording here is garbled). He says Cohu is "forecasting revenue this year in HBM between $15 and $20 million". Asked about timing, he sees those HBM shipments "fairly linear through the year".
quarterly_data.figure: exited 2025 at $11 million HBM revenue; 2026 HBM revenue forecast between $15 and $20 million

quarterly_data.signal: HBM INSPECTION INTENSITY RISES WITH EACH GENERATION: Cohu received a new order for HBM inspection at a customer's engineering lab, supporting development of next-generation memory devices. With each new HBM generation, the requirements on the size of defects to find and on the ball/pillar count to measure increase, and so does the time each inspection takes. players.product: Eclipse thermal test handlers for AI processors, Neon inspection, flexible ATE and PACE analytics software

quarterly_data.signal: Q4 2025 RESULTS (call): CFO says Q4 revenue was in line with guidance at $122.2 million. Recurring revenue (primarily consumables) was 60% of the total and systems 40%. Recurring revenue grew 4% QoQ and 25% YoY. Two customers, one in mobile and one in automotive, each exceeded 10% of Q4 sales, but no customer did for full-year 2025. Q4 non-GAAP gross margin of 40.8% missed guidance because of one-time inventory charges from discontinuing certain product lines and consolidating offerings. The CFO says this refocuses engineering and support resources on high-performance computing, HBM memory and AI-related high-growth opportunities. Q4 operating expenses were $49.8 million.
quarterly_data.figure: Q4 revenue $122.2 million (30% year over year); recurring 60% of revenue; gross margin 40.8%

quarterly_data.signal: ORDER MOMENTUM: CEO says Q4 systems orders rose 47% quarter over quarter, bucking seasonality. Two customers (neither named) drove the increase: a leading analog and mixed-signal semiconductor customer placed higher equipment orders, and a top automotive and industrial semiconductor manufacturer renewed its investment. The systems orders were mainly handlers and thermal subsystems, which Cohu typically sells for mobile processor system-level test, plus some mixed-signal and RF testers. Recurring bookings rose 34% sequentially. The drivers were service contracts (including some large annual contracts that spread across 2026), plus interface products and handler spares, which track utilization. Ten customers were approximately 63% of Q4 bookings, and full-year 2025 orders rose 29% year over year.
quarterly_data.figure: systems orders up 47% quarter over quarter; recurring bookings up 34% sequentially; ten customers approximately 63% of Q4 bookings; 2025 orders increased 29% year over year

quarterly_data.signal: TEST UTILIZATION RISING: CEO estimates that semiconductor test utilization (printed in the transcript as 'test serialization') rose a point to 76% at December, despite a seasonally slow quarter. By segment, compute was 78%, auto 75%, industrial 77%, mobile 72% and consumer 76%. IDMs were a little over 76% and OSATs a little over 75%. For Q1 he notes Cohu does not typically forecast utilization, but thinks it may go up a bit. OSATs may rise faster than IDMs, mobile may cross 75%, and compute should keep rising. (The segment and IDM/OSAT detail appears under an 'Operator' label in the transcript, but it is management's reply.)
quarterly_data.figure: test utilization up a point to 76% at December; compute 78%, auto 75%, industrial 77%, mobile 72%

quarterly_data.signal: Q1 2026 GUIDANCE: CFO expects Q1 revenue to be seasonally flat with Q4, at approximately $122 million plus or minus $7 million. The mix should be about 60% recurring and 40% systems. Gross margin should return to the corporate average of approximately 45% because the one-time Q4 inventory charges will not recur. Operating expenses should stay flat at about $50 million. On systems, the CFO says Cohu has "about 70% of our guided revenue in backlog coming into Q1, with a majority of the balance being shipped in Q2", so system shipments show up in Q1 and Q2. Management is modeling another growth year in 2026 after 13% revenue growth in 2025, and notes that recurring revenue has now risen sequentially four quarters in a row.
quarterly_data.figure: Q1 revenue approximately $122 million plus or minus $7 million; gross margin approximately 45%; about 70% of our guided revenue in backlog

quarterly_data.signal: GROSS-MARGIN LEVERAGE MODEL: The CFO referenced analyst consensus of roughly $130 million a quarter for Q2 and Q3 (an analyst figure the CFO repeated, not guidance). At that level, he says gross margin should reach the high-46% range (46.7%, 46.8%). At about $150 million per quarter it would stay just under 48%. At what management currently sees as the normalized run rate, about $160 million a quarter, gross margin would be 48%.
quarterly_data.figure: gross margin 46.7%, 46.8% at the consensus revenue level; just under 48% at $150 million per quarter; 48% at about $160 million a quarter (normalized run rate)

quarterly_data.signal: ECLIPSE HIGH-POWER THERMAL HANDLER FOR AI DEVICES: In Q4 Cohu closed its first order for a high-performance thermal configuration of the Eclipse handler, supporting a customer's AI device roadmap. The CEO describes it as an even higher power version of its TCORE thermal control on an Eclipse handler. Cohu had been qualifying the system with the customer (not named), and the first real production unit shipped in late January. He would not disclose 2026 volumes. He says Cohu has forecasts for ramping production from more than one customer and has the capacity to ship those systems this year. He expects the Eclipse shipment rate to increase in Q2 going into Q3, describing 'a ramp heading to the middle of the year'. He also sees a strong forecast for the Eclipse line going into compute and mobile applications. (The transcript prints parts of this CEO answer under analyst names.)

DATA-CENTER POWER AND PHYSICAL-AI DESIGN WINS: Cohu won its first mixed-signal tester order at the analog and connectivity business unit of a large semiconductor manufacturer, extending Diamondx beyond earlier wins. The CEO says a large mixed-signal automotive supplier (not named), won a little over a year ago, is now deploying the tester in two of its three major business units. It is one of the top six or seven automotive semiconductor manufacturers. Devices now running on Cohu testers include digital controllers and PMIC devices used in data center racks and on boards around large GPUs. He expects at least one of these tester design wins, on the digital controller side, to accelerate toward the middle of the year. Cohu also booked a multiunit order for a new handler still in development, targeting automotive ADAS and physical AI device test and separate from the Eclipse/GPU opportunity. An initial qualification system ships this summer, with follow-on units later in the year. Cohu also booked tri-temperature handlers across multiple customer sites for growing power module test demand. (The data-center PMIC answer appears under an 'Operator' label in the transcript, but it is management's reply.)

BALANCE SHEET / CAPACITY FUNDING: CFO says cash and investments rose by $286 million in Q4 to $484 million at year end. The increase came from the convertible notes offering and cash from operations. The notes raised gross proceeds of $287.5 million at a 1.5% interest rate, with a 32.5% conversion premium, a five-year term and a capped call up to $41 per share. Total debt is $305 million, and the net proceeds add liquidity for strategic initiatives. Full-year 2025 capital expenditures were $21 million, including $9 million to buy the Malaysia factory in Q1. The CFO says the company is now well positioned to support the business ramp and anticipates normal maintenance capex each quarter this year (2026).
quarterly_data.figure: cash and investments $484 million; convertible notes $287.5 million; 2025 capex $21 million including $9 million for the Malaysia factory
